text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Each cell is the feature group's share of the arm's total split gain, averaged over plants and folds. Gain here is XGBoost's split importance: how much a column's splits reduce the training loss. Split gain is not the error gain over B0 shown in the other figures.'
text.tspan: Each cell is the feature group's share of the arm's total split gain, averaged over plants and folds.
Gain here is XGBoost's split importance: how much a column's splits reduce the training loss. Split gain is not the
error gain over B0 shown in the other figures.

g.aria-label: Gradient legend titled 'Mean share of split gain' for fill color with values from 0.0 to 0.9

g.font-family: Matter Semi Mono, Roboto Mono, monospace

text.aria-label: Title text 'The split gains come from a separate refit of each arm as a single-value (not quantile) XGBoost model. Gain is measured on training rows. Gain also divides credit between correlated columns by chance. Importance is never evidence that an input helps; the planned contrasts are the evidence. Arms. AN: the analogue ensemble: the mean, clear-sky index and spread of the power, rescaled by clear-sky irradiance, on the 5 of the last 30 days whose forecast clear-sky index was closest to the target's. B0: the baseline with no lag. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day- ahead forecast). L2: L1 plus that hour's weather forecast. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its residual at the lag hour.'
text.tspan: The split gains come from a separate refit of each arm as a single-value (not quantile) XGBoost model. Gain is measured on
training rows. Gain also divides credit between correlated columns by chance.
Importance is never evidence that an input helps; the planned contrasts are the evidence.
